labels.label: btzprop:reg_complete
labels.notes: Row stays partial and the module docstring writes the label without the ** mark (SpearFamily.lean:11), which is correct: only step (1) of the sorry of E0RegComplete.regM_isCauchyComplete_of_complete (RegComplete.lean:374) is proved. Read against BTZ_1.tex l.1090-1091 and l.1574. LFSurgeryData (SpearFamily.lean:239-248) is not vacuous. ι is countable, and pt : ι ≃ ↥(S ∩ S0 M) is an equivalence, so the family is empty only when S ∩ sing₀ is empty. Each D i is a full strict E0Surgery.SpearSurgeryDatum: vertex in sing₀ ∩ I⁻(S), S's trace the graph of τ_Σ over the closed disc, in the shaft, plus the complete spacelike cusp of Lemma 2.6(ii). pt_ray puts pt i on the i-th ray at a positive parameter. The fields disjoint (Pairwise Disjoint on spearSet), isClosed (∀ i, IsClosed spearSet), locallyFinite (mathlib LocallyFinite of spearSet) and rimC1 are all real conditions; pt_mem, covers and countable_inter_S0 follow from them. toSurgeryData maps a finite family onto the unchanged strict SurgeryData field for field; finite is the only extra input. Hypotheses: the restriction to E₀ is flagged ⚠ (T-btz-scope), and GH and Cauchy-maximal are carried. Cauchy-completeness is taken as IsE0C1CompleteCauchy (OQ-142), and _of_rimC1 weakens it to IsCauchySurface plus RimC1. RimC1 is verbatim the rim field of both IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy and IsE0C1CompleteCauchy, so it is a projection and not a new hypothesis. The finding (l.1091/l.1574 gap) is faithful. l.1091 justifies disjoint spears only through Cauchy-compactness (finitely many lines). l.1574 asserts disjoint spears for the complete case without argument. The REPORT presents this as a filled gap, not a counterexample, and that is accurate. It refines the ledger's existing finding that « applies as is » (l.1571) fails.

findings.what: exists_spearSurgeryDatum, exists_spearSurgeryDatum_cover and exists_shrink are near-verbatim copies of the strict GX.E0Surgery.exists_spearSurgeryDatum (Surgery.lean:2901), exists_spearSurgeryDatum_cover (:3178) and SpearSurgeryDatum.exists_shrink (:2920). The only change is the hypothesis: (IsCauchySurface S, RimC1 M S) in place of IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy. No name clash at graduation: they live in the distinct namespace GX.E0SpearFamily, the file elaborates with `open E0Surgery`, and exists_shrink is a root-namespace theorem, not the dot-notation SpearSurgeryDatum.exists_shrink. But the duplicated proofs can drift apart, and two declarations with the same short name invite ambiguity wherever both namespaces are opened.
findings.fix: At graduation, generalise the strict lemmas to take (hS : IsCauchySurface S) (hrim : RimC1 M S), with RimC1 moved into GX.BTZ.Surgery. Re-derive the IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy forms from them in one line and delete the copies here.
